args.rationale: This patient has MRSA bacteremia with infective endocarditis. He developed new chest pain and went into cardiogenic shock. Echo showed new LV wall-motion abnormalities and a pericardial effusion that progressed to tamponade. Emergency pericardiocentesis drained yellowish, turbid fluid. Coronary angiography then showed disruption of the prior stent and a rapidly enlarging coronary pseudoaneurysm. This fits an infected coronary stent with a mycotic pseudoaneurysm, which carries a high risk of rupture. Drainage and IV antibiotics will not control this infection, so he needs emergency surgery.
args.followup_or_handoff: Send directly to the cardiac OR for the emergency sternotomy already ordered. The planned operation is to resect or ligate the pseudoaneurysm, remove the infected stent if feasible, bypass the affected coronary territory, wash out and drain the pericardium, and assess the valves with debridement or replacement if needed. Until then, give mechanical and inotropic support as needed and keep the pericardial drain in place. Continue IV anti-MRSA antibiotics and avoid thrombolytics and systemic anticoagulation apart from what is needed during surgery. Pericardial fluid Gram stain, culture, and cell count, and serum troponin, were not available in the source, so send these and follow up the results. Infectious diseases should be involved to set the length of antibiotic treatment. After surgery, admit to the cardiac ICU with repeat blood cultures and echocardiography.
